leah (devex):hey team — customer on Node seeing event-stream responses cut off after a few tokens when behind corp proxy. root request 200 but SSE ends prematurely. any fast guesses? :confused:

sam (sdk): do they have a small repro? node example + whether proxy is CONNECT or transparent would help. is python also failing?

leah (devex): attached sanitized snippet from their capture:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked
data: {"id":"a1","delta":"hi"}
<socket closed by midstream>
```
Only when proxy is in path. Python client reportedly stays open.

jorge (eng-runtime): typical culprit: corporate TLS inspection that re-signs certs + a proxy that rewrites Connection headers. That can turn a streaming keep-alive into a closed socket. Any Via/X-Forwarded headers?

leah (devex): yes: `Via: 1.1 corp-inspect` and proxy adds `Connection: close`.

sam (sdk): Node specifics: a mutating Connection header can cause the http.Agent to destroy the socket. Quick checks: 1) verify Node trusts the corp CA (NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS or compiled-in trust). 2) enable DEBUG logging (REDWOOD_DEBUG=network) and listen to res.socket events to see whether we get 'end' or 'close'.

leah (devex): they said they added CA to system store but didn't restart Node. also tried curl streaming and it failed too (with --no-buffer).

jorge (eng-runtime): system store updates sometimes require a restart; and some Node builds ignore system store and need NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS. For proxies that intercept TLS, try raw CONNECT passthrough (bypass inspect) to confirm. Use openssl to inspect issuer:

```
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example:443 -proxy proxy.corp:3128
```
Look at `issuer=` and `Verify return code`.

sam (sdk): workaround suggestions for Node:
```
const HttpsProxyAgent = require('https-proxy-agent')
const agent = new HttpsProxyAgent({
  host: 'proxy.corp',
  port: 3128,
  ca: fs.readFileSync('/etc/ssl/corp_inspect.pem'),
  cert: fs.readFileSync('client.pem'),
  key: fs.readFileSync('client.key'),
  keepAlive: true,
  maxCachedSessions: 0 // try to avoid TLS session reuse bugs
})
new Redwood({ agent })
```
If proxy requires mTLS on the CONNECT, certs must be applied to the proxy agent (not the downstream TLS) — that's a common gotcha.

leah (devex): they tried adding certs to proxy agent and it improved stability but still intermittent. proxy logs show `backend reset by peer` around the same times.

jorge (eng-runtime): backend reset hints our load balancer or app pool closed the connection when proxy behaved oddly. We should gather ingress logs and connection-level traces (X-Request-Id / trace ids). Opening infra ticket.

sam (sdk): extra debugging: capture pcap locally with tcpdump: `tcpdump -w stream.pcap host api.redwood.example and port 443` — sharing pcap (sanitized) shows which side closed first. Also try toggling HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1 — some proxies mishandle long-lived HTTP/1.1 chunked streams.

leah (devex): customer asked for simple mitigations to try now. I suggested: 1) bypass proxy for streaming host (if allowed), 2) set NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS + restart Node, 3) use proxy agent with certs and maxCachedSessions:0, 4) try python client as a temporary fallback.

ops-bot: created infra ticket INF-2034 to correlate ingress logs and proxy traces (linked to thread 1805554321).

leah (devex): thanks — sending steps to customer and will attach ingress trace when infra responds. :thumbsup:

sam (sdk): we should add a short DevEx note: "Node streaming + corporate proxies: checklist (NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, proxy agent certs, maxCachedSessions, tcpdump steps, openssl commands)". i'll open a docs PR after infra updates.

leah (devex): awesome — i'll follow up once I have the infra logs. :pray:
